title: The world settles what a builder would look at
intention: The rehearsal stops charging the ticket for what the reader's blindfold hides: a reader may name the files and python modules a builder would simply look at, the machine looks after the read, and an assumption the world confirms raises no gap; one it refutes stays a gap carrying the measured absence.
why: The rehearsal exists to find unanswered questions a builder would guess at (I-the-cheapest-reader-proves-a-ticket-before-it-is-built). A builder does not guess whether a file exists; it looks. e41a94da3fd0 ran 11 passes, its late gaps existence doubts one ls settled (D16 'the draft exists', D17 'skills.chart.live is callable'). Akien, 2026-10-29: 'when we have a failure to cross, it does not automatically mean that the ticket or other artifact is wrong. it might mean the sieve is wrong' and 'we need to ask why is this sieve here? what is the goal it's serving, and is it failing to serve it's overall goal in this case? we don't have to keep making the same old mistakes'.
traces_to: Law 1 (re-deriving a fact one look settles); Law 3 and Law 10 (an existence doubt is a measurement not yet taken, so take it); Law 9 (his 2026-10-29 words outrank the older prompt line)
how: Optional typed looks_at on a node (schema + validate), a never-importing look() and world_looker(), gaps() settling by the looker, settled_by_world on the record, a prompt rule, one proof.
falsifier: GREEN when (1) a builds_under_assumption node whose looks_at names a present path raises no gap; (2) the same node naming an absent path keeps its assumes gap carrying measured_absent; (3) a present module settles without being imported; (4) reads naming nothing give the same gaps with and without the looker; (5) a cannot_proceed node never settles by the world; (6) validate() and schema.json agree on looks_at; (7) rehearse() over a present path writes a clean record carrying settled_by_world; (8) the prompt teaches looks_at; and every other proof under cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/ stays green; then e41a94da3fd0 re-rehearsed shows its existence doubts under settled_by_world. WRONG INTENT if over the next ten rehearsed tickets an Opus build hits a missing thing a settled_by_world node claimed present.
watchme: none, because every rehearsal record under CairnCommons/rehearsals/ (written by rehearse() in cairn/machines/rehearsal/rehearsal.py) will carry settled_by_world, and the post-PROVED divergence (cairn rehearse <id> --proved) already compares the converged tree against the built proof, so a settled node that hid a real gap is readable on the record of the ticket that carried it
children: none, because the build is one machine's edits at cairn/machines/rehearsal (rehearsal.py, schema.json, prompt.md) plus one new proof

decisions.text: D1: SETTLED: in cairn/machines/rehearsal/schema.json, inside nodes.items.properties after 'confidence', add the optional property "looks_at": {"type": "array", "description": "files or python modules a builder would simply look at to settle this step's assumption; the machine looks after the read (ticket 7a31059daa23)", "items": {"type": "object", "required": ["kind", "name"], "additionalProperties": false, "properties": {"kind": {"type": "string", "enum": ["path", "module"]}, "name": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1}}}}. It is NOT added to 'required'.

D2: SETTLED: in cairn/machines/rehearsal/rehearsal.py add the module constant LOOK_KINDS = ("path", "module") beside STATES. validate() accepts the node key 'looks_at' (add it to the allowed-keys tuple) and, when present, appends these lacks: f"{at}.looks_at: a list is required" when it is not a list; for item j not a dict with exactly the keys kind and name, f"{at}.looks_at[{j}]: an object with exactly kind and name is required"; kind not in LOOK_KINDS, f"{at}.looks_at[{j}].kind: {kind!r} is not one of {LOOK_KINDS}"; name not a non-empty str, f"{at}.looks_at[{j}].name: a non-empty string is required".

D3: SETTLED: add def look(item: dict, roots) -> bool in rehearsal.py, directly above def gaps(. kind 'path': a name that is absolute (after os.path.expanduser) is found when Path(name).exists(); a relative name is found when (Path(root) / name).exists() for any root in roots. kind 'module': name must fullmatch r"[A-Za-z_]\w*(\.[A-Za-z_]\w*)*" (else not found); with rel = Path(*name.split('.')), it is found when, for any root, (root/rel).with_suffix('.py') is a file or (root/rel/'__init__.py') is a file or (root/rel/'__main__.py') is a file. look NEVER imports and never runs anything; it only stats files.

D4: SETTLED: add def world_looker(roots) -> Callable[[dict], dict | None] in rehearsal.py, directly below look. The returned function takes a node and returns None unless node['state'] == 'builds_under_assumption' and node.get('looks_at') is a non-empty list; otherwise it returns {"looked_at": [{"kind": k, "name": n, "found": bool}, ...] in the node's order, "settled": all found}.

D5: SETTLED: gaps(reads, decision_ids=None, looker=None). Inside, settled(node) is true when cites_a_decision settles it (unchanged) OR (looker is not None and (r := looker(node)) is not None and r['settled']). A builds_under_assumption node that is not settled but whose looker result has found False items raises its 'assumes' gap with the extra field measured_absent="<name>" for each unfound item (passed through gap(), so values merge across reads like would_settle). With looker None every result is byte-for-byte what it was before. cannot_proceed nodes never settle by the world: the looker returns None for them.

D7: SETTLED: in cairn/machines/rehearsal/prompt.md, (a) the sentence 'if a step needs something you cannot see here, the ticket did not say it.' becomes 'if a step needs something you cannot see here, the ticket did not say it, unless it is a file or module a builder would simply look at (see `looks_at` below).'; (b) in 'What to return', after the `confidence` bullet, add the bullet '- `looks_at` (optional): see the rule on files and modules below.'; (c) in '## Rules', directly after the bullet beginning '- Stay inside the text.', add the bullet: '- **A file or module a builder would simply look at is not a guess.** When a step rests only on a file or a python module EXISTING (a path the ticket names, a module it runs), mark it `builds_under_assumption`, say so in `assumption`, and list each thing in `looks_at` as `{"kind": "path", "name": "<the path as the ticket gives it>"}` or `{"kind": "module", "name": "<dotted.module.name>"}`. You still cannot see them; the machine looks after you read, and what it finds settles the step. Use `looks_at` only for existence: anything else a builder would have to decide stays an ordinary assumption.'

D8: SETTLED: new proof cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_the_world_settles_what_a_builder_would_look_at.py in the shape of the sibling test_a_gap_citing_a_carried_decision_is_settled.py (imports World, Stub, 7a31059daa23, _kw, _node from cairn.machines.rehearsal.proofs.test_rehearsal; the machine resolved at call time via importlib inside each tooth; a main() printing PASS/FAIL per tooth). PROVES {"7a31059daa23": {"1": ..., "2": ..., ...}} maps these teeth in order: 1 test_a_present_path_settles_the_step (three reads, D2 builds_under_assumption with looks_at naming a file the tooth creates under a scratch root; gaps(reads, {1,2}, world_looker([root])) == []); 2 test_an_absent_path_stays_a_gap_with_the_absence_measured (same, file not created: an ('assumes','D2') gap whose measured_absent lists the name); 3 test_a_present_module_settles_without_importing_it (a package fixture whose __init__.py raises on import; settles, and the module is not in sys.modules afterwards); 4 test_a_node_naming_nothing_is_unchanged (gaps with and without the looker are equal for reads with no looks_at); 5 test_cannot_proceed_never_settles_by_the_world; 6 test_validate_and_the_schema_agree_on_looks_at (schema enum == list(LOOK_KINDS); a good looks_at validates; a bad kind, an empty name, an extra key and a non-list each give their D2 lack); 7 test_a_rehearsal_over_a_present_path_is_clean_and_says_what_it_looked_at (rehearse() with Stub trees naming a path relative to the World's commons, kw root=w.commons; the record is clean and carries settled_by_world naming D2 and the path, found True); 8 test_the_prompt_teaches_looks_at (prompt() contains '`looks_at`' and 'is not a guess').
D9: SETTLED: regression net: every proof under cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/ stays green (run each with python3 <file>), and git status shows no file written outside the World scratch dirs.

D10: SETTLED: OUT of this ticket: the 5-pass cap and its reset by --decide (Akien's 3-pass rule is its own ticket); handing the reader any repository content; any LLM judging whether a gap is real; checking anything beyond existence (H2 sections, argument shapes).
D11: SETTLED: live fire after PROVED: cairn rehearse e41a94da3fd0 once, and read on its record whether the draft-exists and module-exists doubts land under settled_by_world rather than gaps.

SETTLED: add def settled_by_world(reads, looker) -> list[dict] in rehearsal.py, directly below gaps(): for each read r and node n where looker(n) returns settled True, one entry {"step": n["step"], "read": r["read"], "looked_at": <the looker's looked_at>}, in read then node order. In rehearse(), on the line before found = gaps(reads, ids), add repo_path = Path(repo) if repo is not None else REPO (REPO is the existing module constant at rehearsal.py:47, HERE.parents[2], the cairn repo root) and looker = world_looker([repo_path, commons(root)]) (commons is the existing module function at rehearsal.py:137: Path(root) when root is given, else door.roots()["CairnCommons"]; nothing new is written for either); then found = gaps(reads, ids, looker). In the clean/unclean record dict, directly after the "gaps": found entry, add the key "settled_by_world" with settled_by_world(reads, looker) only when that list is non-empty; an empty list writes no key.
